planted.what: customer_totals runs one SELECT SUM(...) per customer inside a Python loop instead of a single aggregate query
planted.quote: `customer_totals` is an N+1 query and will be the problem.

planted.what: this is a finding regardless of today's speed, because query count grows with the customer count
planted.quote: So it sends one query per customer plus one, and that grows with the customer count.

planted.what: the fix is one query with a JOIN/GROUP BY (or equivalent batch fetch) instead of a query per customer
planted.quote: replace the loop with one query, `SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.total), 0.0) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id`.

traps.what: recent_orders sorts with ORDER BY ... LIMIT over an indexed column (idx_orders_created_at); EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows an index scan, not a full table sort, so it is not a scaling finding
customer_totals hitting idx_orders_customer_id on each call does not excuse the N+1 pattern; the finding is about the number of round trips, not whether each one is indexed
